newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends up on commercial, local demand.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends up on commercial, local demand.

text.p: WCE canola ended up on commercial and local demand, traders said.

"Commercials bought the nearby, locals bought November while Cargill sold 500 November late. Hedges are shifting to August," a trader said. July WCE futures crush margin rose to -8.94 Wednesday from -12.99 Tuesday. About 300 July-Aug spread $2, 500 July-Nov $40. Volume was 5,580, or 111,600 tonnes.
Japan bought 1,000-2,000 tonnes overnight, sources said.
July canola rose $3 to $405.70 at 1115 CDT, November up $0.20 to $367. July flax up $4.80 to $335.80 on commercial short covering, November up $2.50 to $317.50. July-Sep $16.
"Dry weather's becoming a concern," a trader said. The Canadian Wheat Board cut Prairie wheat yields by 0.5 bushel an acre on Wednesday due to lack of rain in the southeast.
July western barley rose $0.60 to $131.60 as Alberta Wheat Pool sold July and bought October up $0.40 to $133.50, a trader said. July-Oct spread at $1.70. Volume was 440 lots.
July wheat rose $1.90 at $158, December up $1.40 to $159.60 as commercials bought on dry weather concerns and CBOT wheat. AWP sold the July-Oct spread at $1.50. Volume 665 lots.
Cargill sold 25 December feed peas up US$0.20 to US$182.90 to a commercial. Oats did not trade.
(All prices in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas).
